statement.p: Find the vertices and foci of the conic section \left(\frac{x - 2}{6}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{y - 5}{4}\right)^2 = 1
The foci are at F_1= (,) (left) and F_2=(,) (right)
Note: Write the vertices from left to right, in an increasing order, starting with the vertex with the lowest x-value.

static.solution:
{\left(\frac{x}{6}\right)}^{2}-{\left(\frac{y}{4}\right)}^{2}=1. For this hyperbola, a=6, b=4 and c=\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{4}^{2}}\approx 7.211.
Hence, the foci are at \left(7.211, 0\right) and \left(-7.211, 0\right)
and the vertices are at \left(6, 0\right) and \left(-6, 0\right).
Since the given hyperbola is obtained by translating the center of the hyperbola {\left(\frac{x}{6}\right)}^{2}-{\left(\frac{y}{4}\right)}^{2}=1 to the point \left( + 2, + 5\right),
the foci are at {F}_{1}=\left(7.211 + 2, 0 + 5\right)=\left(9.211, + 5\right) and {F}_{2}=\left(-7.211 + 2, 0 + 5\right)=\left(-5.211, + 5\right)
and the vertices are A=(6 + 2, 0 + 5)=(8, + 5) and {A}^{\prime }=(-6 + 2, 0 + 5)=(-4, + 5).
